+The written task asks for the meaning of electrification, connected to the Soviet historical example, and an explanation of obtaining, transmitting, and applying electrical energy.
+
+Electrification means widespread use of electrical energy in production, transport, and daily life. It is not merely building generating stations, laying transmission lines, or owning one electrical appliance. Generation, transmission, and application are connected but different functions.
+
+In the Soviet example as presented in this lesson, constructing generating facilities expands the electrical energy available for production and daily life. Generating facilities provide electrical energy; transmission facilities deliver it to the places where it is needed; electrical equipment converts the delivered electrical energy into the other forms needed by the activity. The definition also includes transport. No claim about a particular historical railway, city, station ranking, or present-day grid is needed or supported here.
+
+The coherent relationship is: generating facility supplies electrical energy -> transmission facility delivers electrical energy -> equipment at the use site converts it to the required form. Energy is converted, not created from nothing. Identifying just one of these stages does not explain the whole process. The physical definition is a process involving energy provision, delivery, and use, not a political equation.
